title: OpenAI Introduces ChatGPT Wallet for Agent-Led Payments
summary: OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Wallet, a payment feature that allows AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users without accessing their actual card details. Users will continue to transact directly with merchants, which retain control over pricing, fulfilment, returns, and customer service. “ChatGPT Wallet marks our first American Express Agentic Commerce Experiences integration, enabling eligible Card Members to use their Amex Card while reviewing and approving each purchase,” said Luke Gebb, EVP and Head of Global Innovation at American Express.

title: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect
summary: New York is gearing up to enforce one of the country’s most significant AI safety laws. The state opened a registration portal Tuesday, with which large frontier AI developers like Anthropic and OpenAI will be required to register by January 1, 2027. The RAISE Act , New York’s safety and transparency bill, kicks in at the start of the year. In October, Hochul signed a separate chatbot safety law for minors, restricting behaviors like deceptive human-like interactions, emotionally manipulative or sycophantic responses, and encouragement of behaviors like suicide or disordered eating. Other states have also passed similar AI safety and transparency bills to the RAISE Act. California’s SB 53, which took effect in January, mandates that frontier AI labs have in place and publish safety frameworks, enact whistleblower protections, and report critical safety incidents within 15 days.

title: PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery
summary: David Turturean, a recent MIT graduate and a member of the technical staff at the startup lab Physical Superintelligence (PSI) , used early access to Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model to solve an 18-year-old problem about quantum computing. “I’m totally accepting the idea that this might be the last paper I ever put out,” Turturean, who deferred plans to pursue a master’s at MIT’s prestigious computer science and AI lab to join PSI, told TechCrunch. “In a few months, like, why would you even put out a paper?” The problem in question, the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, concerns the ability of quantum computers to solve problems faster than classical ones. Scott Aaronson, one of the two researchers who posed the problem, writes that he doesn’t quite understand the proof but that he believes it’s correct because it was autoformalized in Lean, a coding language for math, and explained by a team of top researchers with whom PSI shared the solution.

summary: Google is notching up its chipmaking game as the company seeks to reduce its dependence on chips made by other companies for its cloud computing business. Google on Monday unveiled two new variants of its tensor processing units (TPUs), in-house-developed chips meant for AI workloads, that broaden its chip portfolio to additional use cases: confidential inference and more memory capacity for large workloads. The new units, TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, are part of the company’s eighth generation of chips introduced in April this year, and build on what those chips offered, which was more inference capacity and support for large training requirements. title: Mitra-v2: Scaling synthetic pretraining for tabular foundation models
summary: Tabular foundation models promise to end that cycle: one pretrained model reads the labeled rows of a previously unseen table and predicts the rest, with no training run in-between. Last year we introduced Mitra , a tabular foundation model pretrained entirely on synthetic tables. Tabular foundation models work the same way. Mitra-v2's new hybrid SCM prior builds a single causal graph in which each relationship can be a small neural network, a decision tree, a smooth function drawn from a Gaussian process, or a time-dependent autoregressive process, so one synthetic table can carry the mix of relationships found in real tables. Mitra-v2 shows that a tabular foundation model can make substantial gains by widening the diversity and range of its synthetic pretraining, without a deeper network. The fine-tuned classification and regression models and code are open on Hugging Face and ready to use, and we invite researchers and practitioners to try Mitra-v2 on their own tables.

title: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production
summary: NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korea’s leading open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom , K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research , Solar Open 2 from Upstage and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies . As models grow beyond the capacity of a single GPU, they must be split across multiple GPUs, requiring careful coordination of request routing and communication to maintain performance. NVIDIA Dynamo is an open source, distributed inference-serving framework built to deploy models in multi-node environments at data center scale. It handles this routing and communication to maximize inference performance. Optimized for NVIDIA B200 GPUs, these recipes take the guesswork out of deployment, delivering up to 2x performance out of the box. They help developers bring Korea’s open models into production faster and turn them into broadly accessible AI for All services.

title: Why GCCs and Indian IT are Partnering at Enterprise Scale
summary: India’s global capability centres (GCCs) are taking on larger technology, product development and innovation mandates, raising questions about whether multinational companies will increasingly build capabilities in-house at the expense of Indian IT services firms.
